> Quarto publishes websites (like the one you are viewing this on), in addition to dashboards, presentations, documents, books, manuscripts, etc. They utilize .qmd files, which are the "next generation" R markdown files.

# Getting Started making a website

> Quarto tips via [Quarto.org](https://quarto.org/docs/websites/)

## YML File

-   Every Quarto website has a `_quarto.yml` config file that provides website options as well as defaults for HTML documents created within the site. For example, here is the default config file of a simple site:

    ```         
            project:
              type: website

            website:
              navbar:
            background: primary
            search: true
            left:
              - text: "Home"
                href: index.qmd
              - talks.qmd
              - about.qmd
    ```

-   Anytime you add a new `.qmd` file to the project directory, you must "register" it in the file that acts as the skeleton of the entire website body, `\_quarto.yml` for it to actually appear on the website. Do **NOT** change the name to anything but `\_quarto.yml`

-   **Indentation matters**. The "project" section creates the website. The "website" section can contain a footer, navbar, sidebar, etc. Within each of these sections (which are delineated by indents) you add QMD files by:

```         
- text: "optional title"
  href: path/to/.qmd file 
```

-   

    ```         
    If you want to add a drop down feature, instead of adding text:, you add:
    ```

```         
- section:
  href: [optional path to .qmd file]
  contents:
    - text: "optional title"
      href: path/to/.qmd file 
```

-   In these sections you can also customize the sections via adding logos or background colors.

-   If you add - text: "---" in between items in a sidebar, a very neat horizontal line is placed in between items on a sidebar.

-   **Do not forget to add .qmd at the end of the path in a yml file!!**

## .QMD File Tips

-   **Format to add a picture:** \![ \](site/media/ \_\_\_\_\_\_.png).

-   Pages are edited in source mode with markdown. You can use the buttons in the text editor to assist with formatting. - [Github Markdown Guide](https://guides.github.com/features/mastering-markdown/) - [General Markdown Guide](https://www.markdownguide.org/getting-started/)

-   QMD Files can include a header that looks like this:

```         
---
title: PAC Environment & Integrations
id: pac
css: ../../styles.css
author: Madison Ostermann
date: "08/06/2024"
date-modified: last-modified
draft: true
---
```

-   If you designate a title in both the YAML file and the QMD file, the YAML file text will take precedent in the sidebar tab but the QMD file text will take precedent as the title of the actual file when you click on it in the site.

## Building the Website

-   In RStudio, click on **Build** in the upper right corner (in between "connections" and "git"). Then click "Render Website" and wait for the site to render locally. ![](/site/media/render-website.png)
-   In Positron, ensure you have the `index.qmd` file selected, and either click the "Preview" icon in-line with the file tabs, or use the `Shift + Cmd + K` shortcut (on Mac at least). The preview should appear in the viewer pane to the right of any open files, but you can also open up the `localhost` URL in your browser.

# Publishing Website on PositConnect

If you want to publish on your own:

-   Via RStudio Console, with project open

```         
    rsconnect::addServer(\
    "INCLUDE LINK",\
    name = "INCLUDE SERVER ID")
   
    rsconnect::connectApiUser(\
    server="SERVER ID",\
    account="USERNAME",\
    apiKey="PROVIDEDAPIKEY")
```

-   Via Positron Terminal

    -   Ensure that you're in the directory of the project where `index.qmd` is located.
    -   Enter `quarto publish connect`.
    -   When prompted for "Server", enter server id.
    -   When prompted for "API Key", enter the one provided.

-   To publish the website to the Posit Connect Server:

    -   Press the publish button (the blue button with the circle in the middle in the upper right hand corner next to the run button). **MAKE SURE YOU PUBLISH FROM INDEX.QMD!** **Publish button** ![](/site/media/publish.png)
    -   Click on Posit Connect.
    -   Click on publish website with source code.
    -   Enter a Posit Connect Account public URL
    -   Connect your account on posit
    -   If publish from account is empty or you run into an **error** where the "server appears to be valid, but rejected the request to authorize an account" (and have a windows computer), try this:
        -   In the console of RStudio, write the following commands:

            rsconnect::addServer(\
            "<url>",\
            name = "server id")

            rsconnect::connectApiUser(\
            server="serverid",\
            account="myusername",\
            apiKey="YOURAPIKEY")
    -   The website should be uploaded to the posit server!

# Using R/Python/HTML/CSS with Quarto

## Examples

-   A cool feature of Quarto is that you can use / embed multiple coding platforms into it, including HTML, CSS, Julia, R, Javascript, Python, etc.
-   You can embed R scripts like this one:

```{r}
#| label: fig-airquality
#| fig-cap: "Temperature and ozone level."
#| warning: false

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(airquality, aes(Temp, Ozone)) + 
geom_point() + 
geom_smooth(method = "loess")
```

## How to: R/Python/Julia

-   First, in your markdown code include \`\`\`{=r} or {=python} or {=julia}
-   Then, for whichever language, code as normal. Make sure to close the code block with \`\`\`
-   **Important Note:** Make sure you update the renv environment for the PositConnect server. To do this, download necessary packages via your RStudio Console and write `renv::snapshot()`

## How to: CSS/HTML

-   HTML and CSS are used for styling. HTML information is to be included in a code block, similar to how R would be included. CSS information is to be included as its own document.

### CSS

-   For a CSS document (i.e. yourtitle.css ), make sure to include css: path/to/yourtitle.css within the header on your Quarto document. For example:

```         
---
title: PAC Environment & Integrations
css: ../../styles.css
---
```

-   Within the .css document, functions are named to include certain styling that are then called in the .qmd file through :::functionname. An example:

```         
**Located in .css file:**

.hello-output {
  background-color: white;
  border: 1px solid #dee2e6;
  max-height: 660px;
}

**Located in .qmd file:**
::: hello-output
Guidelines and examples surrounding data visualization.
:::
```

-   If you want to change something globally on the website, make your change in the styles.css file that is associated with the index.qmd. For example, you can customize the size of the navigation bar, link colors, title colors, etc. for every page of the website.

-   Pretty much, anything you *cannot* do through simple Quarto commands in the YML file, you can likely do using CSS.

-   [CSS Style Guide](https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/the-css-handbook-a-handy-guide-to-css-for-developers-b56695917d11/)

-   Some CSS styling is "baked" into Quarto, like callouts and learn more. So, no extra, manual steps for that - all you need to do is clarify `:::callout-<type>` or `:::learn-more` and make sure to close when finished.

### HTML

-   HTML acts fairly similarly to CSS but is embedded within the QMD document as a code block. For example, here is how you would change the size and color of a title:

```         

/`/`/`/{/=html/}
<style>
  .styled-text {
    color: #79A742;
    font-size: 55px;
    margin-left: 75px;
  }
</style>

/`/`/` 

<h1 class="styled-text">

Welcome to <br>Analytics Knowledge Base

</h1>
```

-   Make sure to close your text using \</\[however you choose to open it\]\> similar to how you close your code blocks or css styling. Look at the example above for guidance.

-   There are a LOT of options with HTML, including the ability to embed JavaScript with HTML to allow for interactivity. If you would like a more comprehensive example of the features of HTML in Quarto, please refer to my [index.qmd](../../../index.qmd) code.

-   [HTML Handbook](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn/Getting_started_with_the_web/HTML_basics)

### Styling Guide

-   Simple button example using CSS:

```         
.simple-button {
    display: inline-block;
    padding: 15px 20px;
    background-color: orange; 
    color: white; 
    text-decoration: none;
    border: 2px solid orange; 
    border-radius: 15px; 
    font-size: 17px; =
    text-align: center; 
}
```

-   More complicated button example using HTML where the button turns different colors when hovered:

`{{=html}}   <a href= PATH/GOES/HERE"      style="display: inline-block; padding: 15px 20px; background-color: #F16125; color: #ffffff; text-decoration: none; border: 2px solid #F16125; border-radius: 15px; font-size: 17px; text-align: center; transition: background-color 0.3s ease, color 0.3s ease;"      onmouseover="this.style.backgroundColor='#F8B092'; this.style.color='#ffffff';"      onmouseout="this.style.backgroundColor='#F16125'; this.style.color='#ffffff';">     [TEXT ON BUTTON HERE]   </a>`

# Building a Quarto presentation

-   [Quarto presentations](https://quarto.org/docs/presentations/) can be very simple.

-   Quarto supports a variety of formats for creating presentations, although revealjs is recommended, including:

    -   revealjs — reveal.js (HTML)

    -   pptx — PowerPoint (MS Office)

    -   beamer — Beamer (LaTeX/PDF)

-   In markdown, slides are delineated using headings (by dividing slides into sections with \# and into slides with ##, as well as delineated using ---). For example, here is a simple slide show with two slides:

```         
---
title: "PA Knowledge Base Progress"
format:
    revealjs:
        theme: [serif]
        slide-number: true
        show-slide-number: speaker
        chalkboard: true
        code-line-numbers: false
        preview-links: auto
author: "Ally Burg"
date: 07/19/2024
---

## Project Goal

**Build a Quarto website to store Wiki and OneNote documents, as well as act as a knowledge base.**

## Completed tasks

-   Organized and condensed Wiki and OneNote documents
```

-   Quarto presentation templates are very useful and easy, and can include transitions and themes. Further information is located on [Quarto.org](https://quarto.org/docs/presentations/revealjs/).
